This is the prosecution of accused Pawan Kumar pursuant to charge sheet filed by PS Khyala U/s 380/411 IPC subsequent to the investigation carried out by them in FIR No. 533/2019.

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution, on 18.12.2019 at about 7:45 AM at C-23, second floor, Karampura, Moti Nagar within the jurisdiction of PS Moti Nagar accused person committed theft of articles belonging State vs . Pawan Kumar @ Sunny on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97260635/
1 to the complainant from the aforesaid dwelling house and at the same date time and place he was found in the possession of the articles i.e one ladies bag, one mobile phone make Redmi and a cash amount of seven  757/-, aadhar card, pan card belonging to the complainant and his mother and the same were dishonestly received or retained by the accused person.
Accordingly, after the investigation, police filed the present charge sheet against the accused for commission of offence punishable u/s 380/411 IPC.
3. Complete set of charge sheet and other documents were supplied to the accused.

After hearing arguments, charge for offence punishable under section 380 IPC and alternatively u/s 411 IPC was framed against the accused on 10.02.2020 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

MATERIAL EVIDENCE IN BRIEF:
4. The prosecution in support of present case has examined four witnesses in total.
5. PW1 Shiv Kumar deposed that on 18.12.2019 at about 7:45 AM at his residence his mother was inside the washroom and at the same point of time he saw that one person was fleeing away from their residence towards the stairs and he was having in his possession one dark brown/blackish bag which belonged to his mother.

On seeing this, he shouted and started chasing the said person and when he went outside towards the road, he saw one constable namely Harish the came at that place and on hearing the commotion the accused was nabbed.

He further stated that after apprehending the accused person, the bag belonging to his mother was recovered and it was found containing one mobile phone make redmi 6A, Rs.757/-, Pan Card and Aadhar Card belonging to his FIR No.
533/2019, PS MOTI NAGAR State Vs. Pawan Kumar @ Sunny u/s: 380/411 IPC mother and one photograph.

Naresh.
He further stated that he was aware that the bag belonged to his mother as he used to see her carry the same everyday.

He further stated that the accused was taken to PS immediately after apprehension by the said Constable and he was also called at the PS.

The witness further deposed that he reached back at his residence from the PS at State vs . Pawan Kumar @ Sunny on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97260635/
2 about 11 AM.

sentences.text: The witness denied the suggestion that nothing was recovered from the possession of the accused, he further denied that the accused was falsely implicated due to some quarrel with the accused person.

6. PW2 HC Harish deposed that on the day of the incident he was on patrolling duty and at about 7:50 AM he saw one person running with one ladies bag and another person was chasing him shouting 'chor chor pakdo pakdo" and he further stated that on this he apprehended the person who was carrying the said bag and correctly identified the accused person as the person who was carrying the said bag.
The witness further deposed that the person who was chasing the accused person disclosed his name as Shiv Kumar and he informed him that the accused had stolen the said bag from his house.
The information was given to PS and after some time, ASI Satyawan reached at the spot and the accused was handed over to him along with the ladies bag.
The witness further deposed that public persons were asked to join the proceedings but none joined.
Upon apprehension, the bag was checked and articles as aforesaid were found in the same.
He thereafter deposed on similar lines as PW1.
He further stated that the IO prepared the rukka and after the registration of FIR, he came back to the spot and handed over the same to the IO.
The witness further stated that accused was arrested and his personal search was conducted vide personal search memo Ex.PW2/A.

Thereafter accused was interrogated and made a disclosure statement which is Ex.PW2/B the witness further deposed that after completion of the aforesaid proceedings case property was deposited at the malkhana and they returned to the PS.
The case property was also correctly identified by the witness.

During his cross-examination the witness depose that he was conducting patrolling duty on his government motorcycle however he did not remember whether the registration number was mentioned in the departure entry or not.
The witness further stated that he remained present at the spot till 8:30 AM till the IO reached the spot.

He further stated that the IO reached the spot on FIR No. 533/2019, PS MOTI NAGAR State Vs. Pawan Kumar @ Sunny u/s: 380/411 IPC his private motorcycle and he recorded the statement of the complainant however he did not record the statement of the mother of the complainant in his presence.

sentences.text: PW2 further deposed that he left along with the Rukka at about 10:10 AM.
He stated that the distance between the spot and the PS is of about 200 to 250 meters.
The witness further deposed that the seizure memo was prepared in one go after the registration of a FIR.
He stated that the complainant did not accompany him to the PS and stated that the disclosure statement of accused person was recorded at the spot.
Lastly the witness stated that the site plan was prepared in his presence which is Ex. PW2/DA1.
The witness admitted that their vehicle have not been shown on the site plan.
The witness denied the suggestion that the same have not been shown as he was not present at the spot.
7. PW3 SI Satyawan is the IO of the present case who deposed that on the day of the incident he received DD No.16B regarding the apprehension of one person near post office Karampura.
Thereafter he reached the spot and found that Ct. Harish was present at the spot along with the complainant and he produced the accused with one ladies bag.

The accused was correctly identified State vs . Pawan Kumar @ Sunny on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97260635/
3 by the witness, thereafter he deposed on similar lines as PW-2.
He additionally stated that he prepared the Rukka which is Ex. PW3/A and the witness correctly identified the case property.
During his cross-examination, the witness stated that he reached at the spot at about 8:30 AM on his private motorcycle vide DD No.16B.
The witness admitted that the registration number of the same is not mentioned in the said DD entry.
The witness further stated that the distance between the PS and the spot is about 1.5 kilometres.
He further stated that besides Ct. Harish and the complainant, 4-5 other public persons were present at the spot.
He further stated that he did not inquire from any other public person about the incident, however, public persons were asked to join the preceding but they refused.
The witness further stated that he prepared the seizure memo before the registration of a FIR.

sentences.text: PW4 SI Daya Ram deposed that on the date of incident he was working as duty officer and duly exhibited the DD number 16 B dated 18.12.2019 which is Ex.PW4/A (OSR) received in regards to apprehension of a boy along with the stolen bag and stated that investigation regarding the same was marked to ASI Satyawan.

He further stated that he registered the present FIR which is Ex.PW4/B and made endorsement on the Rukka which is in his own handwriting Ex PW4/C and stated that the same was handed over to Ct Harish and duly proved the certificate under section 65B of Indian evidence act.
He proved the present case FIR by bringing the original FIR register and DD register.
The witness was not cross- examined despite opportunity given.
9. No other PW was left to be examined, hence PE was closed.

STATEMENT OF ACCUSED U/S 313 Cr.P.C.
10. Statement of accused recorded separately U/s 313 Cr.P.C in which all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence were put to him.
The accused controverted and denied the allegations levelled against him and stated that he has been falsely implicated in this case.
Accused opted not to lead any defence evidence.

ARGUMENTS:
11. Ld. APP Mr. Rajesh Kumar for State has argued that prosecution witnesses have supported the prosecution and their testimony has remained un-rebutted.
That on a combined reading of testimony of prosecution witnesses, offence U/s 380/411 IPC is proved beyond doubt.
12. On the other hand, Ld. Legal Aid Counsel Mr. Sanni Garg, for accused have stated that there is no legally sustainable evidence against the accused.
It is argued that the accused has been falsely implicated by the complainant.

Arguing further, Ld. counsel stated that there are material FIR No.
533/2019, PS MOTI NAGAR State Vs. Pawan Kumar @ Sunny u/s: 380/411 IPC contradictions and inconsistencies in the testimony of prosecution witnesses rendering them unreliable and unconvincible.

4 FINDINGS:
13. Arguments adduced by Ld. APP for State and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused have been heard.
Evidences and documents on record perused carefully.
14. I have bestowed my thoughtful consideration to the rival submissions made before me.
Accused Pawan Kumar @ Sunny is indicted for the offences U/s 380/411 IPC.

Section 380 IPC provides:-
"Theft in dwelling house, etc.--Whoever commits theft in any building, tent or vessel,
which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or used for the custody of property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine".

Section-411 IPC provides:-
"Dishonestly receiving stolen property.--Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be stolen property,
shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both".

15. Firstly, the purchase bill of the stolen mobile phone is on record which matches with the description of the mobile phone as mentioned in the seizure memo and the same is in the name of the complainant.
Also, the testimony of PW-1 regarding the details of items stolen matches with that of PW-2 and 3 and the testimony of all the witnesses in this regard has remained un-reubutted.
Further, Ex.PW1/C shows the time of arrest FIR No. 533/2019, PS MOTI NAGAR State Vs. Pawan Kumar @ Sunny u/s: 380/411 IPC as 11:45 am which is shortly after the alleged commission of offence.

sentences.text: All the witnesses have corroborated each others' testimonies and there is no material contradictions among them.

16. The main argument of the defence has been that the mother of the complainant has not been arrayed as a witness in the case while the property belonged to her and that there is no other public witness besides the complainant.

It is settled law that no particular number of witnesses is required to prove an offence and Non-joining of public witnesses is of no consequence where the evidence of prosecution witnesses is otherwise cogent, convincing, reliable and creditworthy.

[Sec 134, Indian evidence act and Chander V/s State of Haryana (2013) 14 SCC 420, Gian Chand & others Versus State of Haryana (2013) 14 SCC 420, Ram Swaroop Versus State ( Govt. of NCT of Delhi) (2013) 14 SCC 235, State ( Govt. Of NCT of Delhi) Versus Sunil (2001) 1 SCC 652 and Hari Lal Versus State (NCT of Dehli) 1995 SCC Online Del 212 & Raja Vs. State (1997), 2 Crimes 175 (Del.) relied upon.

]. 
The prosecution shall must be able to show that a movable property was taken out of its lawful possession.
The complainant remained un-contradicted regarding the presence of accused at his house as he saw him running down from the stairs of his house with the bag.
The articles were stolen from his house which would show the lawful possession of the complainant over the said articles.

In view of the aforesaid, non-joining of the mother of the complainant as a witness is of no consequence otherwise also she is stated to have been in the washroom when the said occurrence State vs . Pawan Kumar @ Sunny on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97260635/
5 had taken place.
17. Further, The DD entry by which the IO had proceeded for investigation was duly proved by producing the DD entry register.
18. The Defence has further argued that PW1 has stated that he reached back at his residence at about 11:00 am however, the arrest memo shows the time of arrest as 11:45 am, but

in the opinion of this FIR No. 533/2019, PS MOTI NAGAR State Vs. Pawan Kumar @ Sunny u/s: 380/411 IPC Court,
this fact alone cannot be construed such as to doubt the entire prosecution story, when there is other clinching evidence against the accused.

sentences.text: It is settled law that slight variation may arise when the witnesses is examined after lapse of time.
The witness was examined on 23.02.2023 and the incident is stated to have taken place on 18.12.2019.
Defence counsel has also failed to point out any material contradiction in the testimony of the prosecution witnesses.

The minor contradictions are only in regards to the distance between the spot and police station as stated by PW-2 and PW-3 and that the PW-1 has stated that Ex. PW2/DA1 was not made in his presence and it is not even the case of prosecution that the same was prepared at the instance of PW-1, therefore, the same does not even amount to a contradiction.
It is a well- settled preposition of law that there always is some possibility of variations in the exhibits and occular evidence, and it cannot be ruled out.
But it is not every minor variation or inconsistency that would tilt the balance of justice in favour of the accused.

Only where contradictions and variations are of a serious nature, which apparently or impliedly are destructive of the substantive case sought to be proved by the prosecution, they may provide an advantage to the accused.

[ Dayal Singh &
Others Versus State of Uttranchal (2012) 7 SCALE 165, Radhakrishna Najesh Versus State of Andhra Pradesh (2013) 11 SCC 688, and Umesh Kumar Versus State of Bihar (2013) 4 SCC 360;State of Karnataka Vs. Suvarnamma, Supreme Court, Crl. Appeal No. 785 of 2010 dated 14.10.2014; A. Shankar v. State of Karnataka, AIR 2011 SC 2302 relied upon].

upon a perusal of the testimony of the prosecution witnesses, no such material contradictions are found as to impeach the credibility of version of the prosecution.

20. Furthermore, Not only the testimony of material witnesses have gone un-contradicted, the accused has only raised a bald defence u/s 313 Cr.P.C. i.e., a defence of plain denial without explaining any circumstances FIR No. 533/2019, PS MOTI NAGAR State Vs. Pawan Kumar @
Sunny u/s: 380/411 IPC surrounding the offence.

sentences.text: It was upon the accused to state as to how he came to be upon the spot or why the present case was lodged against him.
It is not the case that the accused was known to the complainant or the police officials had any enemity against him.
Section 106 of Evidence Act states that, "when any fact is especially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him".
The failure of accused to explain there circumstances is a further link in the chain of circumstances which makes is complete.
[Nar Singh Versus State of Haryana (AIR 2015 SC 310), and Raj Kumar Singh versus State of Rajasthan (2013) 5 SCC 722 relied upon].

21. In view of the observations given above and the evidence led on record, this Court is of the view that the prosecution has successfully proved the case and established the offence charged against the State vs . Pawan Kumar @ Sunny on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97260635/
6 accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Hence, the accused Pawan is found to be guilty for the offence U/s 380 IPC.
Since, the main offence has been proved and the accused was apprehended while he was making an attempt to flee from the spot the question S.411, IPC does not arise.

Accordingly,
accused Pawan Kumar @ Sunny S/o Sh. Raj Kumar, R/O: H. No. WZ-183, Basai Darapur, Delhi stands convicted for the offence U/s 380 IPC.
